what_it_is.prose: The Embraer C-390 Millennium (military designation KC-390) is a Brazilian twin-turbofan medium transport and tanker aircraft. It is not in Indian service, but it is one of the leading contenders in the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme — a competition to replace the ageing Antonov An-32 and legacy Avro HS-748 fleets with 60 aircraft (with options for more) in the 18–30 tonne payload class, valued at roughly ₹1 lakh crore (~$10.5 billion). The IAF issued the MTA Request for Proposals on 12 August 2026. Embraer is bidding in partnership with India's Mahindra Group: the two signed a memorandum of understanding in February 2024, elevated it to a strategic partnership in October 2025, and in February 2026 unveiled a proposed in-country MRO ecosystem (base/heavy maintenance, structural inspection, component overhaul, avionics support and training), positioning India as a potential regional C-390 support hub. Under the MTA's Make-in-India terms, initial aircraft would be delivered fly-away with subsequent airframes built domestically at a minimum 40% indigenous content rising toward 60%. The C-390 carries up to 26 tonnes at cruise speeds up to 470 knots, is powered by two International Aero Engines (IAE) V2500 turbofans, and can perform cargo/troop transport, air-drop, aerial refuelling, medical evacuation and firefighting. It is in service with Brazil, Portugal, Hungary, the Netherlands and South Korea. India relevance here is therefore competitive/industrial rather than operational: no order or induction has occurred as of August 2026.

deployments_procurement.summary: The C-390 is not in Indian service. Its India footprint is as an MTA-programme contender bid by Embraer with Mahindra: an MoU in February 2024, a strategic partnership in October 2025, and a proposed local MRO ecosystem in February 2026. The IAF's MTA RFP (60 aircraft, ~₹1 lakh crore) was issued on 12 August 2026; no selection or order has been made.

Where a C-390 final assembly line would be located in India, and the Mahindra work-share, are not defined.

import_dependencies.summary: As the C-390 is not in Indian service, dependencies are prospective: a Brazilian-origin design with US/European engines and systems, against MTA terms requiring 40%→60% indigenous content and local MRO to be built via the Mahindra partnership.

faq.question: Is the Embraer C-390 in Indian service?
faq.answer: No. As of August 2026 the C-390 Millennium is not in Indian service and has not been ordered by the IAF. Its India relevance is as a contender in the Indian Air Force's Medium Transport Aircraft (MTA) programme, bid by Embraer in partnership with India's Mahindra Group.

faq.question: What is the Embraer–Mahindra partnership for the C-390?
faq.answer: Embraer and the Mahindra Group signed a memorandum of understanding in February 2024, elevated it to a strategic partnership in October 2025, and in February 2026 proposed an in-country MRO ecosystem (heavy maintenance, structural inspection, component and avionics support, training) to position India as a regional C-390 hub — aligned with Make-in-India requirements that any MTA winner build aircraft locally at 40% rising to 60% indigenous content.
